text_no_role_has_read: (The full paper reports its landmark rates only to 48 months — its figure legend says so — which is why the five-year rates above come from the ASCO 2026 abstract of the same analysis rather than from the paper.) This is what "an encouraging trend" looks like underneath, and it is why the trend is labelled exploratory.
Also of the five-year survival rates, 92.2% against 71.3%, and the intervals on both.
Because for a hazard ratio, 1.0 means no difference at all.
It contains two: the three-year paper reports a hazard ratio of 0.425 on nine deaths, with an 80% interval of 0.179 to 1.004, beside the five-year 0.471 on fourteen.
It is a figure from 157 patients in an open-label study, not the result announced this month — and it describes a rate of recurrence or death, not a share of patients cured.

Morning Glory Sciences — a specialist outlet, and we give its argument on its merits — the Phase 2b population was stage IIIB–IV, the Phase 3 adds node-negative disease, and “absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower, so the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit.” Pharmacy Times makes the opposite case about the same patients: resected stage IIB or IIC melanoma “can face risks of recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality similar to those observed in stage III disease.” Neither reading appears in any of the general coverage we hold.
Reference Survival Analysis — StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf Source for the direction of a hazard ratio either side of 1.0.
Registry CheckMate 238 — ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02388906 Source of the arm labels quoted in the text.
Registry INTerpath-001 — ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05933577 Checked 2 September 2026.
Registry KEYNOTE-054 — ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02362594 Pembrolizumab against placebo.
Registry KEYNOTE-716 — ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03553836 Pembrolizumab against placebo.
Source of the five-year landmark rates, 68.8% against 49.1% recurrence-free.
Source of the quoted 1-sided alpha of 0.1 per protocol , which is the threshold the trial set for itself, and of the three-year figures HR 0.510, 95% CI 0.288–0.906.

The coverage is listed because the piece makes claims about what it said — and, in one case, because a hazard ratio reaches this page only as something quoted inside it, which is the subject of the paragraph that quotes it.
The full paper reports its landmark rates only to 48 months, which is why these come from here.
The source for what a hazard ratio measures and why 1.0 is its no-difference value.

This trial's own threshold is on the record: the three-year paper says the trial was designed with approximately 80% power to detect a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.5 against a one-sided alpha of 0.10, and the ASCO 2024 presentation of the three-year data, which we hold, states the same threshold in its own words — 1-sided alpha of 0.1 per protocol .
